findings.statement: False rejections, pay effects, individual restoration, and compensation remain outside the public denominator.

observations.statement: The ICO issued nine enforcement notices covering more than 2,000 workers at 38 facilities.
Facial recognition and fingerprint attendance processing affected attendance and pay administration.
Workers were not offered a clear alternative in the public enforcement account.
The organisations were ordered to stop specified processing and destroy unneeded biometric data within three months.
General ICO guidance separately requires false-acceptance, false-rejection, threshold, bias, and alternative-access controls.
The bounded public search recovered no independent post-deadline verification or complete worker-level pay and access restoration record.

open_questions: Was the correction implemented at the operative system boundary?
Were affected records, access, pay, duties, or accounts restored?
Was implementation independently verified after the deadline?
Did exits, silence, deterrence, overturns, restoration, and compensation enter later validation?
title: Serco Leisure: cessation and destruction order versus compliance proof
